nodes.label: project.yml (XcodeGen manifest)
nodes.rationale: Generates Genesyx.xcodeproj declaratively so the project file never needs to be hand-edited or committed in a fragile state.

nodes.label: Release signing configuration
nodes.rationale: Archiving signs MANUALLY with the App Store distribution profile because Automatic signing tries to mint a Development profile first and Apple refuses; set on the target rather than the xcodebuild command line because a command-line setting leaks into every SPM package target (GoogleSignIn, AppAuth, ...), which don't support provisioning profiles at all.

nodes.label: Genesyx iOS README
nodes.rationale: v1 is local-only (on-device storage, mock auth) as the simplest, fastest App Store path; every repository takes an optional backend so turning Supabase on later requires no call-site changes.

nodes.label: iOS Learn Parity Handoff (missing)
nodes.rationale: File does not exist in the repo; Learn build is blocked at a 'READBACK GATE' waiting on this handoff doc plus articles.json and a hero-images folder path.

nodes.label: Partner Invite Email Setup
nodes.rationale: Universal Links (associated-domains) intentionally left switched off: enabling the entitlement breaks the Xcode archive (provisioning profile lacks the capability), and serving genesyx.co.uk links before the AASA file is hosted would send new invitees to a 404 instead of the app.

nodes.label: statpearls-urinalysis citation (removed)
nodes.rationale: Removed because it supported the urine-based pH model, which no longer applies after the vaginal pH migration.

nodes.label: push_enabled default-false migration
nodes.rationale: profiles.push_enabled defaulting to true server-side is harmless since the client already gates on iOS authorization, but the migration was only written (not applied) because Android/web clients that read the column may treat false differently and needed confirmation first.

nodes.label: Optional Brand Fonts README
nodes.rationale: Shipping app uses Apple's system font and declares no unbundled UIAppFonts; brand fonts (Outfit/Inter) are documented but withheld until the design adopts them.

nodes.label: App Store Submission Pack
nodes.rationale: Canonical, paste-ready submission doc created so the repo doesn't maintain two conflicting App Store listings.

nodes.label: Apple App Store Release Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Genesyx v1 kept local-only (no backend/login/analytics/ads) so the App Privacy label can be the simplest possible answer ('Data Not Collected') and review stays fast; backend added only in a reviewed v1.x.

nodes.label: Supabase Wiring (deferred)
nodes.rationale: SupabaseBackend.swift is wrapped in #if canImport(Supabase) and excluded from the build until the package is linked, specifically so the deferred remote layer cannot break the local-only v1 build.

nodes.label: Supabase Edge Functions README
nodes.rationale: Privileged operations (accept invite, unlink partner, delete account) cannot run from the app with the anon key and require the service role, so they are implemented as Supabase Edge Functions rather than client-side calls; functions are stubs with intended logic that must be reviewed against the real schema/RLS before deploying.

nodes.label: Bug #1: sign-out state leak
nodes.rationale: Sign-out wiped cycle, pH and daily logs but left milestone flags and the read-article list behind, so on a shared/resold device the next user inherited them: her celebrations were already marked spent and would never fire, and Learn nudges silently skipped articles she never opened.

nodes.label: delete_account Edge Function
nodes.rationale: Native apps can't hold a service-role key, and App Store Guideline 5.1.1(v) requires in-app account deletion, so deletion runs server-side as an Edge Function called with the user's JWT.

nodes.label: PhInsightLogic
nodes.rationale: Filters to vaginal-only readings before computing; all-legacy input returns the empty state so legacy urine rows are never classified under the vaginal model.

nodes.label: PhRepository
nodes.rationale: New readings are always written as vaginal; rows/records missing measurement_type decode as urine for legacy tolerance — never defaulted to vaginal, to avoid misclassifying old data.

nodes.label: PhStatus (vaginal model)
nodes.rationale: Migrated urine pH to vaginal pH because Genesyx tracks vaginal (not urine) pH clinically; the two-band Healthy(<=4.5)/Elevated(>4.5) model replaces acidic/optimal/alkaline since urine-collection guidance and citations no longer applied.

nodes.label: MedicalSource
nodes.rationale: Added to satisfy App Store Guideline 1.4.1, which requires citations wherever the app makes health/medical claims.

nodes.label: BUG-1: hydration card tap conflict
nodes.rationale: The hydration card's whole-card background/onTapGesture was winning taps over the inner Sources-footer button, so tapping the row navigated to Track instead of expanding Sources; fixed by moving tap-to-open-Track to an outer .contentShape + .onTapGesture so inner buttons win.

nodes.label: PartnerRepository
nodes.rationale: Linking accounts does not expose cycle, log, or pH data to the partner under the current owner-only health-data RLS policies — health records stay private even between linked partners.

nodes.label: PartnerRepository
nodes.rationale: acceptPartnerInvite, unlinkPartner and deleteAccount need the service-role key which native apps can't hold, so they are implemented as Supabase Edge Functions called with the user's JWT.

nodes.label: CycleEngine
nodes.rationale: Settings are projections and do not learn a new average from historical period events because the current model stores one settings row, not a period-event history.

nodes.label: NotificationPlanner
nodes.rationale: Caps reminders to a gentle cadence and avoids negative language about a missed streak.

nodes.label: Bug #3: wrong invite code shared
nodes.rationale: The device invented its own 16-character code for instant UI feedback while the server generated a different one, so any link built from the device's code redeemed nothing.

nodes.label: Bug #4: optimistic partner link on refusal
nodes.rationale: accept() set partner optimistically before the server replied; the server correctly refuses a code addressed to someone else (HTTP 403) but the app showed a linked partner anyway.
nodes.norm_label: bug #4: optimistic partner link on refusal

nodes.label: Genesyx/Notifications/NotificationPlanner.swift
nodes.rationale: Designed so a broken streak is never named in copy, and 14 silent days trigger exactly one hand-back message then silence, so the app never nags.

nodes.label: "Is it real?" Fix Pass Report
nodes.rationale: Reverted the re-enabled Pregnancy entry point because Apple Guideline 2.1 (App Completeness) rejects placeholder 'Coming soon' content while v1.0 was actively in review, overriding another concurrent session's change.

nodes.label: Project Status & Inventory
nodes.rationale: trg_ph_readings_updated_at trigger deliberately kept (not dropped) even though server-side it makes pH sync last-push-wins, because the real conflict protection (unsynced local edit always beats server) lives client-side in PhSync.merge.

nodes.label: Bug #2: invite never sent
nodes.rationale: Typing an email created a database row but nothing else — no email was sent, no link was shared, the code never left the device, so the invite feature was a form that did nothing.

nodes.label: CalendarDate
nodes.rationale: An integer day abstraction, used to avoid time-of-day and daylight-saving errors in streaks and day-keyed records.
